questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Career opportunities, cultural exchange, and the opportunity to meet new people and build meaningful friendships were central to my choice of study destination. I was motivated by the possibility of gaining international experience that could strengthen my academic profile and future career prospects, while also immersing myself in a different cultural environment. Experiencing everyday life in another country, learning from new perspectives, and expanding my social network were all important factors in making the decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it difficult to make friends, especially with the Czech students, which made it harder to feel fully integrated into the social environment. I was also somewhat disappointed by the lack of structure and formality at Charles. Courses and activities were largely planned individually by professors, and there seemed to be limited coordination or oversight from the institution. In some cases, this created situations where student well-being and safety did not feel sufficiently considered or supported.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The emails we received from the Erasmus programme and Charles University were clear and helpful, and they provided the practical details necessary to get started. This made the transition smoother and gave a good overview of what to expect in the first weeks.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was very limited assistance upon arrival. Most of the practical aspects had to be handled independently, and there was little direct support or guidance on site beyond the information provided beforehand.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find off-campus housing. I found my apartment through Flatio, and the process was straightforward and smooth. The platform was easy to use, communication was clear, and everything worked out very well in practice. I also had a very positive experience with my landlord, who was helpful and reliable. I would recommend using platforms like Flatio and starting the search early to secure a good option.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Living off campus can be a great experience, but it requires a bit more independence and planning.

It can also feel more isolating compared to living in student housing, since you are not surrounded by other exchange students in the same way. Making an effort to join social activities, classes, or student groups can help with this. On the positive side, living off campus often provides more comfort, privacy, and a more authentic experience of everyday life in the city. Starting the housing search early and using trusted platforms is strongly recommended.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not choose the housing provided to students, as the dormitories did not seem to meet my expectations in terms of comfort and living conditions. Instead, I arranged accommodation independently off campus, which worked out much better and suited my needs more closely.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was stressful and somewhat chaotic. It followed a “first come, first served” system, which meant there was no guarantee of getting the courses you needed. This created a lot of pressure and uncertainty. I also had to take responsibility for securing some mandatory courses myself, which made the process more demanding and time-sensitive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The available help was quite limited. There was some general information provided, but practical guidance and direct support during the process were not very strong, which made it harder to navigate things when challenges came up, only the Erasmus office was helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was ultimately successful in registering for the classes I wanted, but it required a lot of effort. I was somewhat lucky, and I had to write several emails and actively request to be registered in certain courses before it finally worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared that you may not get all the courses you initially want, as registration can be competitive and somewhat uncertain. It is important to act quickly, stay flexible, and communicate proactively with professors and coordinators if issues arise.

Also be aware that professors have a great deal of autonomy, both in course planning and grading, and there is typically no external examiner involved. This makes it especially important to understand course requirements clearly and maintain good communication throughout the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, I found the academic level of the courses to be relatively low compared to what I am used to at the University of Copenhagen. The expectations, workload, and depth of the material were not as demanding as I had anticipated, and I was not particularly impressed from an academic standpoint.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCPH, the teaching style felt much more unstructured in many courses. The organization and expectations often depended heavily on the individual professor, which led to a very uneven experience across classes. There was also considerable variation in English proficiency, which sometimes made communication and learning less consistent.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Advanced Macroeconomics 
- International Trade 
- Global Economic History
- Financial Markets

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the International Trade course, primarily because the professor was highly engaged and delivered well-structured, well-prepared lectures. Compared to many of the other courses, the organization was clearer, expectations were communicated more transparently, and the overall teaching quality was noticeably stronger.

The course also created a better learning environment, where it was easier to stay motivated and follow the material. Discussions were more focused, and the professor made an effort to explain concepts in a way that was accessible to international students. Overall, it stood out as one of the few courses where the academic experience felt consistent and rewarding.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any significant unexpected costs. Most expenses were predictable and in line with what I had planned for before arriving, so there were no major financial surprises during the stay.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most everyday expenses were cheaper than I expected compared to Copenhagen. Food, transport, and general living costs were noticeably lower, which made day-to-day life more affordable. The main exception was gyms, which were not significantly cheaper and in some cases were closer to Copenhagen price levels than I had anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They were very limited and not strongly organized by the university. There were few structured cultural, athletic, or social activities specifically aimed at exchange students, so most initiatives had to be found independently,

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would not recommend relying on university-organized activities. Instead, it is better to look for opportunities in the city on your own, such as local events, gyms, language cafés, or social groups, as these are easier to access and often more engaging.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the city’s cultural life. Explore museums, historical sites, cafés, and local neighborhoods, and travel within the country or nearby regions. The cultural environment outside the university is one of the strongest aspects of the experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to adjust at first. I did not find it easy to connect with local Czech students, and I rarely experienced that they were very open or talkative toward exchange students. This made it harder to feel integrated into everyday student life and to build local connections, especially in the beginning.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I unfortunately did not have much success with this myself, as many local students tended to stay within their existing social circles. My advice would be to be proactive early on join group work, attend smaller classes, and take initiative in conversations. It may require more effort than expected, and integration does not always happen naturally.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One of the main challenges was the social distance between local and international students, as well as a more reserved communication style. It sometimes felt difficult to read social situations and know when or how to engage, which made it harder to form connections and feel fully included.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated the city’s cultural life, history, and everyday atmosphere. Prague offers a rich cultural environment with museums, architecture, cafés, and public spaces that make it an inspiring place to live. Even if social integration at the university was challenging, the broader cultural experience of living in the city was very rewarding.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be proactive with course registration and communication with professors, as the process can be uncertain and requires initiative.
2. Do not expect the same academic structure and level as at UCPH; much depends on the individual professor.
3. Focus on the cultural and personal experience of living abroad, as this may be more rewarding than the academic part.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is important to be independent and flexible. Many practical matters, from housing to course selection and daily life, require personal initiative. Starting preparations early and not relying too heavily on institutional support can make the experience smoother.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a new city and experiencing a different culture on a daily basis was the most rewarding part. Exploring Prague, meeting other international students, and gaining a broader perspective beyond my home university made the stay valuable despite some academic and social challenges.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was the lack of structure academically and the difficulty of integrating socially with local students. This sometimes made it hard to feel fully connected to the university environment and required extra effort to create a meaningful experience independently.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
